author: Sharjeel Hashmat
title: August 2026: fewer Dubai home sales, price per square foot barely moved
description: Dubai recorded 11,147 home sales in August 2026, down 35.2% on a year earlier, while median price per square foot was down 1.9%.

body.p: Projectory Research, analysing Dubai Land Department registrations, counted 11,147 Dubai home sales in August 2026, worth AED 21.43 billion. That is 11.5% fewer sales than July and 35.2% fewer than August 2025. Registered value was down 46.5% on a year earlier.
The median price per square foot was AED 1,693, down 1.9% on August 2025.
Off-plan made up 8,270 of the sales (74.2%) and ready homes 2,877 (25.8%). Off-plan registrations fell 10.8% from July, and ready-home sales fell 13.6%.

body.h: A second count of the same month

body.p: Sherwoods Property, also drawing on Dubai Land Department data, reported 11,600 property sales worth AED 27.89 billion in August, an average ticket of AED 2.40 million, with off-plan leading by volume.

The two counts differ. They appear to cover different sets of transactions and I have not checked either publisher's full method, so compare the direction and not the totals. Both show off-plan ahead of ready homes.

The most recent Dubai Land Department release I found covers Q1 2026: AED 252 billion in transactions, up 31% year on year, with 60,303 transactions, up 6%. I did not find an official August release, so the August numbers above are as reported by the two firms and not confirmed by the Department.
Fewer transactions with a nearly flat price per square foot means deal counts moved more than prices. One month does not make a trend.

Before acting on a single month, check whether the fall is in the segment you care about, off-plan or ready, and what the price per square foot has done in your specific building. The citywide median cannot tell you that.

sources.name: Projectory Research: Dubai property market August 2026, DLD home sales report
Sherwoods Property: Dubai real estate transactions August 2026
Dubai Land Department: Dubai real estate transactions reach AED 252 billion in Q1 2026

draftNotes: Every August figure is tier 3. Your own rule says tier 3 cannot be the only source of a headline number. Recommend holding this article until the August figures are checked against DLD open data, or publishing it labelled as reported, which is how it is written now.
Projectory's statement that higher-value sales expanded conflicts with its median sale price falling 19.7%; I did not use either claim.
Sherwoods compares August with June and quotes off-plan share as 68.5% of trailing volume; I used only that off-plan leads by volume.
